title: Observer and Strategy
idea: Observer lets one object announce an event to any number of listeners it never names. Strategy lets an object delegate one decision to a swappable algorithm object.

analogy.text: A newsletter goes to every subscriber on the list; the writer never knows who they are. A sat-nav picks fastest or cheapest route by a setting you change.
analogy.breaks: Real subscribers read later; Java listeners run right away, in order.

points: The subject (the event source) keeps listeners in a `List` typed by one interface.
Firing an event loops over that list and calls each listener in turn.
The context (the strategy's user) holds the strategy in a `private final` field.
Strategy replaces a `switch`, Observer replaces hard-coded calls: each new behaviour is a class.

hero.title: One event out, one rule swapped

steps.caption: `main` passed three listeners to `subscribe`. `Checkout` keeps them in a list typed `OrderListener`.
It loops over the list and calls `onOrderPlaced` on each listener, in subscribe order.
`Checkout` never names a concrete listener. Adding SMS means one new class, no edit here.
Strategy: `Cart` was built with a `ShippingCost`. It asks that object for the cost.
Pass a different strategy and the rule changes. `Cart` code stays the same.
Observer fans one event out to many. Strategy plugs one rule into one slot.

code.title: Observer
code.caption: One event, three listeners. A lambda works because the listener interface has one method.

walk.text: The listener contract: one method, so a lambda can implement it.
The subject holds listeners by interface, never by concrete class.
`subscribe` adds a listener at run time.
`placeOrder` does its own job, then notifies every listener in order.
`main` wires listeners in, including an inline lambda for auditing.

code.title: Strategy
code.caption: Same `Cart`, three shipping rules. The rule is chosen by what you pass in.

walk.text: The strategy interface: one decision, `cost`, plus a name for printing.
Each rule is its own small `record`. `FreeOver` carries its limit as data.
`Cart` gets its strategy through the constructor and never checks which one.
`main` builds a cart per rule and prints each total.

pitfalls: Catch exceptions per listener: one that throws skips every listener after it.
Unsubscribe short-lived listeners, or the subject keeps them in memory as long as it lives.
Skip Strategy when there is one rule and no sign of a second.

quiz.q: What is the third line `StrategyDemo` prints?
quiz.why: The subtotal 40.0 is below the 50.0 limit, so `FreeOver` charges 4.0. A `double` prints with `.0`.
quiz.code:
new FreeOver(50.0)  // cost: subtotal >= limit ? 0.0 : 4.0
cart.total(40.0)    // subtotal + shipping.cost(subtotal)

takeaway: Observer broadcasts an event; Strategy swaps a rule. Both replace edits with classes.

starters: How do I stop one failing listener from breaking the others?
Is a Java lambda enough for Strategy, or do I need classes?
How is Observer different from a message queue?
